facts: As Disney CEO from late 2005, Iger put four options to his board; the last was to buy Pixar outright. The room nearly exploded, but the board let him explore it.
Disney Animation had spent over a billion dollars on films in the prior decade and lost nearly $400 million.
On a call about the video iPod, Steve Jobs told Iger that buying Pixar was not the craziest idea in the world.

At Apple, Jobs wrote Pros and Cons on a whiteboard. His objections included that Disney's culture would destroy Pixar and that Iger's board would never allow it. The Cons list was longer, but Jobs judged a few big Pros more important than many small Cons.
Iger committed to protecting Pixar's culture and offered John Lasseter and Ed Catmull leadership of Disney Animation, with specific culture-protecting terms and a branding arrangement.
The deal was all stock, $7.4 billion, at 2.3 Disney shares per Pixar share; the board approved it 9 to 2 in January 2006 despite Eisner lobbying against it.
On announcement day Jobs told Iger his pancreatic cancer had returned and offered him a way out of the deal. Iger went ahead.

tension: The seller said the buyer's culture would destroy what he sold.
opening_idea: Open on the whiteboard and Jobs's list of reasons against.

lessons.idea: When you take over something good, find out what makes it work and leave that alone; fit it to your systems only where it does not.
lessons.anchor: Jobs's fear that Disney's culture would destroy Pixar

reflect_final: In something you lead or have just joined, what is working well that you are about to rearrange without first asking the people who run it?

use_cases.situation: You have just taken over a team that performs well.
use_cases.move: Ask each person what must not change before you change anything.

use_cases.situation: Two families or two households are merging routines.
use_cases.move: List what each side values most and protect that first.

use_cases.situation: You are bringing a smaller group into your bigger one.
use_cases.move: Say aloud what you will leave alone, and why.

pocket_idea: The seller feared the buyer's culture; the buyer started by asking what he must leave alone.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: Steve Jobs's list of reasons not to sell Pixar to Disney included Disney itself.
conversation_variants.thirty_sec_idea: Bob Iger wanted to buy Pixar, and Steve Jobs had objections: Disney's culture would destroy Pixar, and Iger's board would never agree. Iger sat with him at a whiteboard in Cupertino and went through the pros and cons. The all-stock deal, worth about $7.4 billion, was announced in January 2006.
conversation_variants.question_idea: What have you taken over that you should leave alone?
